The circle-jerk is strong in this thread. Am I gonna be the only one to point out that there are many levels of sweetness when it comes to dark chocolate? The darkness of chocolate is measured by the percentage of cocoa solids in the mix. The higher percentage of cocoa, the lower the percentage of sugar. What most people consider "dark" chocolate usually starts in the 60-65% range, and the percentages go up from there. Most people won't eat anything 80% or above, but there are brands that sell bars that way as candy for people like my girlfriend. Her preferred percentage is 90%. I generally don't enjoy anything past 75-80%, depending on the brand. We both like milk chocolate as well but it's like eating a completely different confection.
